newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Parliament to vote on Israel Aircraft debt accord.
newsitem.headline: Parliament to vote on Israel Aircraft debt accord.

text.p: The Finance Ministry will submit a proposal to the parliamentary finance committee soon that will enable commercial banks to renew their credit line to Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI), ministry sources said.
A company spokeswoman confirmed negotiations were nearing a conclusion.
"IAI is facing temporary difficulties in cash flow because negotiations with the banks over a debt accord have lasted over two years. This is longer than expected," she said.
"Negotiations are taking place now and will be resolved soon. Once concluded, the accord will be brought to the Knesset (parliament)," she added.
Under the proposed accord between the government, banks and state-owned IAI, the banks will redistribute among them the collateral of IAI and reschedule the company's debts.
At the same time the goverment will increase the company's equity by $122 million, enabling IAI to receive new bank loans, the ministry sources said.
The banks will also release $180 million due IAI and frozen in closed accounts because of IAI's debts.
IAI will then be able to pay off its debts to local suppliers, the company spokeswoman said.
She would not disclose the size of the company's debts with the banks or its suppliers.
